correctness.rationale: For all 1<=p<=infinity, diameter of any translate of radius r forces 2r >= max(||a||_p,||b||_p,||a+b||_p), and integer norm shells force the optimum >=2^(1/p-1). Coordinate orthogonal unit frame attains it. For 1<p<=infinity norm threshold admits only signed axis and diagonal vectors; the ordered independent triples a,b,a+b give exactly 24 unimodular possibilities and each packet triangle sits in a unit square. At p=1 the linear L1-to-Linfinity isometry U(x,y)=(x+y,x-y) gives exact circumradius half of the L1 pair diameter: the integer shell of L1<=2 yields 48 ordered frames, of which 24 have |det|=1 and the other 24 have |det|=2, spanning checkerboard parity lattice. Check includes p=infinity, p=1, both packet triangles, unordered counts /2, and frames permitted to have proper sublattice index. Independent exhaustive enumeration of finite shells in independent_checks.py returned (48,24) and determinant split 24+24; source verify.py inspected rather than trusted as proof. Infinite-lattice obstruction derives analytically from integer shell, not enumeration alone.
residual_risks: The count is specific to planar coordinate Lp norms; cannot extend to other lattices/bodies without a new proof.
Finite checks confirm enumeration only after the analytic shell bound.
